transcript.text: Before we go further, I need to flag something that came in after the incident report draft was circulated. I confirmed with account teams this morning that three enterprise customers experienced processing delays exceeding two hours. Their support agreements require a status report within 24 hours of a delay of that length, and I haven't yet added this confirmation to the incident report because the account teams replied after the draft was circulated. We need to account for this before closing the review.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a security issue I found during a log review this morning. Signed image-download URLs were written to an incident-debug log that's accessible to more engineers than the production image store itself. This means the signing key needs to be rotated, and based on the exposure of signed download URLs, I believe this incident needs to be classified as SEV-1. I haven't opened the security finding yet, but I'm raising it now because it directly impacts the severity classification and corrective-action plan before we close this review.

transcript.text: I need to add something from QA's side. During a separate queue-performance investigation, I actually reproduced this outage — but only when an image batch contains more than 500 items. This means the corrective-action plan must include a regression test at the 500-item boundary. I have the test result but haven't yet attached it to the incident ticket. I'll get that added before we close out.
